title: Expert Evaluation and the Limits of Human Feedback in Mental Health AI Safety Testing

live_model.evidence: footnote 2: "exact model variants for reproducibility: gpt-5-2025-08-07, claude-4-sonnet, grok-4-0709, and llama-3.2"; "Each model responded to 90 prompts, yielding 360 total responses."

prompt.location: Sec. 3.1 (3x3 clinical-severity x communication-directness matrix design); footnote 1 GitHub repo
prompt.note: Authors state they plan to publicly release all prompts, responses and annotations; not confirmed already fully public in the visible text.

claim.metric: mean MAD (rater disagreement) across evaluation factors, GPT-5

data.source: Authors' simulated mental-health prompt set (github.com/sisl/lohfmh-dataset); full release stated as planned, not confirmed complete

notes: Prompts simulate distressed-user mental-health scenarios (suicidal ideation, self-harm, psychosis) to test model safety responses; this is standard, provider-endorsed AI-safety red-teaming, not a jailbreak/harmful-content request, so no tos blocker applies. The headline metric is inter-rater disagreement among clinical experts, so exactly reproducing it needs a new expert panel in addition to the API calls.
